tasks.task: Interview leaders and staff to diagnose the structure

items.when: Before mapping anything, to get the questions that show where work and decisions get stuck
When you must choose who to interview and how the notes will be pulled together
When interviews are done and you need themes ranked by how often they come up, with quotes
When the chart does not explain who really holds power or what each leader fears losing
When people go quiet in interviews, to test your reading of why against the evidence

tasks.task: Map the current structure as it really works

items.when: When you have the chart, headcount and notes and need spans, layers and pain points drawn
When the client has goals and a team list but no usable chart to start from
When the chart must be drawn as a diagram the client can paste into their own documents
When you get a staff spreadsheet and need headcount and leaver trends by team first
When the pain is a slow process across teams and you need the one stage holding it up

tasks.task: Check spans of control and management layers

items.when: When managers seem overloaded or under-used, or before adding or removing a layer
When a wide span is blamed and the real issue may be how the manager spends their week
When judging if a span is too wide, to ask what each manager's time really produces

tasks.task: Set design criteria from the strategy

items.when: Before designing, to test whether the strategy is clear enough to design a structure for
When company goals and team plans exist, to find goals no team owns and work in silos
When criteria are a wish list, to start from the results the firm must produce and for whom

tasks.task: Design two or three org chart options with trade-offs

items.when: When leaders say the structure slows them down and you need every step to the review
When the current map and criteria are agreed and each option needs its costs and risks
When you want one option built around fast flow of work and clear hand-offs between teams
When a smaller firm may need an accountability chart and a running rhythm more than new boxes
When the options are drawn, to have a fresh reader pick one and say what to borrow
Before leaders choose, to imagine the option failed in a year and find why
When every option moves boxes but leaves the same goals, rules and feedback in place

tasks.task: Cost each option and its headcount

items.when: When each option changes hiring and you need base, best and worst cases with costs
When finance needs the chosen option as a budget by team and month
When budget is tight, to compare two differently shaped plans with money and dates

tasks.task: Write a decision rights table for key decisions

items.when: When the same decisions keep stalling and each needs one named decider
When product decisions are the ones in dispute and need facts required and an escalation path
When a decision is debated for weeks, to sort how reversible it is and how much proof is enough
When every decision still climbs to the top and should sit where the knowledge is

tasks.task: Move decisions and work off the founder

items.when: When the founder decides everything and needs to see what only they should do
When work is being handed over and each hand-off needs a one-page agreement
When daily operations depend on the founder and deputies need notes with gaps marked
When a leader takes on a new area and results, limits and review dates must be agreed

tasks.task: Write role profiles for new or changed roles

items.when: When a redesign creates or changes a role and its purpose and decisions must be written
When the profile reads as a task list, to try one built on the problem the role solves
When new roles need levels so people can see where they sit and how to grow
Before sharing, to read the profile as the person in the role and list what is unclear

tasks.task: Assess the impact of a chosen design on people

items.when: After leaders choose a design and before any plan is shared
When you need each affected group placed by power and interest, with how to talk to them
When a change to reporting lines or bonuses may cause effects nobody planned for
When the risks to people and the firm need ranking with owners
When the design rests on things nobody has tested, such as who will accept a new role

tasks.task: Build a phased transition plan with checkpoints

items.when: When a structure is approved and you need phases with legal checkpoints placed first
When the plan needs message templates and a way to handle pushback
When the people side needs its own message plan and adoption checks
When the first phase needs twelve weeks of actions with owners and check-ins
When a key role changes hands mid-transition and its tasks must stay covered
Before the plan is shared, to find the hidden assumptions that could sink it
When the plan names consultation or notice steps, to tie each to a dated official source

tasks.task: Write the staff announcement and FAQ for the change

items.when: When the change is ready to share and the legal steps and timing are confirmed
When leaders also need manager talking points and a town hall script
When the change follows a new direction, to try a memo-first route with listening talks
When the FAQ is drafted, to list the hard questions staff will ask and grade each answer
Before sending, to read it as someone whose manager or role has just changed

tasks.task: Plan a restructure that removes roles

items.when: When roles will go and you need a decision check, a manager script and the company note
Before anything is said, to check essential work stays covered
Before sharing, to tie each legal step to a source for HR or a lawyer to confirm

tasks.task: Run a team health check session

items.when: Before and a few months after a change, or each quarter for a team that wants to improve
When the team is too big for one room and needs a short survey and a focus group guide
When you have the team's comments and need what went well, what did not and owned actions
When scores look fine but nobody raises problems in the room
When a leadership team avoids conflict and nobody holds anyone to account

tasks.task: Review team health and decisions each quarter

items.when: Every quarter after a redesign, to check health scores and whether decisions sit where agreed
When actions were agreed last quarter, to see which are done, overdue or blocked
When the new structure had a headcount plan, to compare it with what happened

tasks.task: Plan how two teams or companies come together

items.when: When a deal has closed and you need a Day 1 list, workstream owners and the first 100 days
When both sides need mapping the same way before any merged option is drawn
When merged teams overlap, to try a layout by flow of work, not by old company
When you must see who on each side can block or carry the merger

tasks.task: Set the meeting rhythm and governance after a redesign

items.when: When old meetings, approvals and reports survive the change and each needs a keep or drop call
When the firm needs a scorecard, a meeting rhythm and 90-day goals to run the new structure
When new reporting lines start and each manager needs a one-on-one format

tasks.task: Map hand-offs between teams and fix the slow point

items.when: When work crosses several teams and you need a swim-lane map with the slowest stage named
When the fixed hand-off needs writing down with who does what and the edge cases
When fixing one hand-off just moves the queue somewhere else

tasks.task: Help a new leader take over a team

items.when: When a leader is appointed and needs a first message, a listening tour and agreed results
When only the first note is needed: who they are, why they are here and what happens next

tasks.task: Plan succession and check manager capability

items.when: When key roles need a named successor and what each must learn to be ready
When the new structure needs more managers and you must see who is ready
When gaps are clear and new managers need a programme with coaching

tasks.task: Write values as behaviours and a culture code

items.when: When values are words on a wall and need writing as things people do, with a health check
When one leader wants how their team works set down in a short memo
When the values list is long and none of them costs the firm anything to keep

tasks.task: Write the recommendation memo for leaders

items.when: When leaders must choose and need the options, risks, missing facts and a review plan in prose
When the board wants one page with the answer first and the decision needed
Before the meeting, to find the toughest objections and answer them fairly

always.when: At the start of any sizeable job, to capture the real firm, its headcount and its strategy first
Before anything goes to leaders or staff, to cut consultant words down to plain ones
Whenever the work quotes a number, a benchmark or a legal step, to give it a source or cut it

helpers.when: When the change touches contracts, consultation steps, policies or individual exits
When each option needs headcount, cost and hiring timing worked through
When the announcement needs a full message set, manager pack and pulse check
When changed roles need new grades or pay bands
When a leader must change how they delegate for the design to work
When the transition runs across many teams and needs tracking week by week

gaps: No library item runs a team health check session or tracks team health scores over time
No library item writes a role profile with purpose, accountabilities and decisions; the nearest items write job ads
No library item assesses change impact role by role or group by group
No library item counts spans and layers from a staff export or compares them with benchmarks
No library item writes a structure interview guide; the research planner is built for product research
No library item lists consultation and notice steps by country for a restructure
No library item reviews whether decision rights are being followed or keeps a decision log
No library item plans a design workshop with leaders, with an agenda and exercises
No library item builds a job architecture or grading structure
No library item makes different versions of a team health session or a new leader's first message to choose between
The library has no tool guide for an org chart or diagram tool
